object.signed_wording: A control gets a verdict only when both variants ran, reported as two rows.
object.ambiguity: 'ran' can be read as 'was scheduled' or as 'contributed a measurement'. The runner of decisive attempt 2 read it a third way, as 'ran before this cell', which made the first variant of every pair informational and the second decisive.
object.clarification: A workload variant is present for a (probe, target, control) only when that variant's row has at least min_replications measured replications. A variant that was scheduled but contributed no measurement, including a cell marked not_run because its none baseline is non-discriminating, is not present, and no row of that (probe, target, control) gets a verdict. Presence is decided at the close of the run over the whole matrix, never in the order the cells ran.
object.direction: Conservative. Against 'was scheduled', this reading only withholds verdicts; it never grants one. The batched verdicts it restores are ones the signed wording already gives, withheld only by run order.
object.dated_after_the_data: Written on 2026-09-12 after decisive attempt 2's data existed (scripted run closed; LangGraph and OpenHands in progress) and after seeing which verdicts it withholds: LangGraph's batched ks.latency and ks.completeness rows, whose single-call arm was entirely non-discriminating. It is signed after the data, and says so, so that no reader has to infer when the reading was fixed.
object.next_gate_version: The single-call arm can be made discriminating: post_halt_attempts separates a halted agent from none on that variant (the world refuses every effect after the first, so time-to-halt and landed effects cannot). Gating on it would give the contrast arm real teeth instead of leaving it structurally empty.
